title: validation-based threshold protocol (no test-set threshold selection)

protocol.statement: All thresholds are selected on the VALIDATION split only and applied unchanged to the TEST split. The test set is never used for threshold (or fusion-weight) selection.
protocol.default_rule: published operating point = est.predict()/svm.predict(): nominal threshold 0.5 on predict_proba[:,1] (random_forest, xgboost) or 0.0 on decision_function (rbf_svm, qsvm_crosslayer, qsvm_zz); test metrics computed from the actual predict() output
protocol.f1_mcc_rule: thr = argmax over validation of F1 (rule f1_val) / MCC (rule mcc_val); candidate thresholds = midpoints between consecutive DISTINCT sorted validation scores plus one below-min cut; first argmax on ties (deterministic)
protocol.fpr_rule: thr = np.quantile(validation BENIGN scores, 1 - alpha), numpy default 'linear' interpolation; alpha = 0.05 (fpr5_val), 0.01 (fpr1_val), 0.001 (fpr01_val); predict positive iff score > thr; realised test FPR reported
protocol.val_metric_value_column: f1_val/mcc_val: the validation F1/MCC achieved at the selected threshold; fpr*_val: the realised VALIDATION FPR at the selected threshold; default: NaN
protocol.dev_grid_protocol: seed-7 dev_multiseed protocol: group_split(groups, y, 0.30, 0.15, 7); train capped group-wise to 3000 (seed 7) -> 3023; test capped to 6000 (seed 8) -> 6000; validation UNCAPPED -> 13920; Xr from cached reduced_s7.npz; quantum = cached trained params + cached K_tr/K_te, K_va computed fresh from statevectors; classical = build_baseline(model, baselines_cfg, seed=7) refit exactly as dev_multiseed._eval
protocol.nextgen_protocol: official NextGen Train(3000)/Validation(600)/Test(2399) from cached assembled.npz; Xr from the published run's cached reduced.npz (BlockReducer fit on Train rows by _stage_reduce); quantum = cached qtrain_binary_full params + cached K_tr/K_te, K_va computed fresh; classical = run_model protocol (build_baseline seed=17 from baselines.yaml, GridSearchCV, folds clamped to minority count) -- seeds unambiguous, so the strict 1e-6 assert IS enforced for NextGen classical models too
protocol.sanity_gates: (i) split-size asserts (3023/13920/6000 and 3000/600/2399); (ii) 256x256 Gram-block parity between fresh statevectors and the cached published K_tr (tol 2e-5, proves param/state parity before trusting K_va); (iii) published-model reconciliation: the re-run model must reproduce the STORED per-window test scores (tol 1e-9 quantum / 5e-6 classical, xgb proba is float32) -- if the re-run inner CV drifts on a near-tie, the published hyperparameters are recovered by exact score-match over the published grid and that model (the published one, bit-verified) supplies BOTH the validation and test scores; every drift event is recorded in sanity.*.model_reconstruction; (iv) per-model test ROC-AUC must equal the published seed-7 CSV row to 1e-6 for every bit-reproduced model; where the published FIT is not bit-reconstructible in this session (observed for the ensemble-tree models; see sanity.*.bit_reproducible=false) the protocol re-run is used, gated at |dROC| < 1e-3 with the exact delta reported
protocol.cv_near_tie_caveat: observed while building this item: the inner-CV model selection is not bit-stable across sessions at identical code+library versions when two grid points are near-tied (e.g. dev_grid/qsvm_zz C=0.1 vs C=1.0 differ by 0.0027 mean CV-AP); the reconciliation gate makes the operating models unambiguous by pinning to the stored published scores

qsvm_zz.drift_note: inner-CV C-selection near-tie: this session's CV ranks the C grid differently than the published session; final model pinned to the C whose full-fit test scores reproduce the stored per-window scores bit-exactly (i.e. the published model itself)

random_forest.drift_note: the published fitted model could not be reconstructed bit-exactly: neither the protocol re-run nor any config of the published hyperparameter grid (at the protocol seed) reproduces the stored per-window test scores. The protocol re-run (identical code path, config and seed) is used instead; its test ROC-AUC is compared to the published value under the soft tolerance with the delta reported. This session-level irreproducibility of the default operating point is itself evidence for using a validation-based threshold protocol.
